title: Regression with AR(1) errors
html:
Let 𝛃𝛆Y=Xβ+ε with rank(X)=p and AR(1) errors.

  1. Cov(εs,εt)=σu2ρ|s−t|/(1−ρ2). Write 𝛆Cov(ε)=σu2Vρ.

  2. (Prais–Winsten transformation.) Let Lρ be the n×n lower bidiagonal matrix with (Lρ)11=1−ρ2, (Lρ)tt=1 and (Lρ)t,t−1=−ρ for t≥2. Then 𝛆Cov(Lρε)=σu2I, so Vρ−1=Lρ⊤Lρ and detVρ=1/(1−ρ2). For known ρ, the generalized least squares estimate is ordinary least squares on (Lρy,LρX), and it is the best linear unbiased estimator.

  3. (Likelihood.) If the errors are normal, the log-likelihood is 𝛃𝛃ℓ(β,ρ,σu2)=−n2log⁡(2πσu2)+12log⁡(1−ρ2)−‖Lρ(y−Xβ)‖22σu2.

  4. (Cochrane–Orcutt.) Let 𝛃𝛃S(β,ρ)=∑t=2n{(yt−ρyt−1)−(x(t)−ρx(t−1))⊤β}2, the sum of squares of the last n−1 rows of 𝛃Lρ(y−Xβ). Alternate the steps 𝛃𝛃ρk+1=∑t≥2etet−1∑t≥2et−12  with e=y−Xβk,βk+1=argminbS(b,ρk+1). Then 𝛃𝛃𝛃S(βk+1,ρk+1)≤S(βk,ρk+1)≤S(βk,ρk), so S decreases along the iterations, and any limit point 𝛃(β∗,ρ∗) with |ρ∗|<1 at which the steps are continuous is a stationary point of S.
